Definition: properly, hurrying; hence (adverbially) in a hurry
BiblicalUsage: Maher means hurrying, quickly, soon, and it is the word for how fast Israel turned aside: Deuteronomy 9:12 says they are quickly turned aside out of the way, and Exodus 32:8 says the same at the calf, while Psalms 143:7 turns the speed the other way, hear me speedily, O LORD.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this word convicts me twice: I turn aside quickly, and I want God to answer speedily, and both speeds say something about my heart.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
